# Applied Craft

> Opinionated analysis of how AI changes the way products are built, decisions are made, and judgment develops. Written for product leaders navigating AI, by Sanidhya Khilnani.

Applied Craft is a blog about the craft of product work in the AI era. Each essay examines a specific frame or tension — judgment, taste, intuition, skill, leverage — and takes a clear position. The essays are long-form, argumentative, and intended to be load-bearing for readers making real decisions about how to use AI in their work.

## Topics

The work clusters around five recurring threads. Three are cognitive faculties (taste, creativity, intuition). One is the master variable that ties them together (judgment). One is the practitioner context (product management in the AI era).

- [Taste](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/taste.html): The evaluative half of how good work happens. A 9-step cognitive loop, supported by the discipline of clearing one's own instrument.
- [Creativity](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/creativity.html): The generative half. Three independently trainable components — intake, processing style, depth of operation — jointly necessary, with the weakest one capping the whole output.
- [Intuition](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/intuition.html): A third mode of knowing, distinct from analysis and from luck. Possibly the one form of cognition AI cannot meaningfully approximate.
- [Judgment](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/judgment.html): The master variable in the AI era. The half of professional skill AI is exposing rather than replacing.
- [Product Management](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/product-management.html): What product management is in the AI era. The four senses haven't changed; what counts within each one has.
- [Topics index](https://appliedcraft.blog/topics/): All topics, with curated essay lists.

## Essays

- [Creativity Isn't Inspiration. It's Three Things. You're Probably Working on the Wrong One.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/creativity-three-components.html): Creativity decomposed into three trainable components: intake (what you're feeding it), processing style (how you work with it), and depth (how far below the articulating surface you can reach). The asymmetric reader is the more creative reader; the unscheduled hour is the most under-funded part of professional life.
- [Taste Isn't Something You're Born With. It's a 9-step Loop You Run.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/the-taste-loop.html): Taste decomposed as a cognitive loop of nine steps across three triads (Receive, Interpret, Resolve). The discipline underneath is clearing the instrument of desire, pride, and ego.
- [Your Intuition Isn't Unfinished Analysis. It's a Different Kind of Knowing.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/your-intuition-isn-t-unfinished-analysis-it-s-a-different-kind-of-knowing.html): Intuition as a third epistemic mode that isn't analysis or randomness. Argues AI can approximate compressed experience but not embodied knowing or the integration of incommensurables.
- [The AI Judgment Trap: Why Getting Better at AI Is Making You Worse at Product](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/the-ai-judgment-trap-why-getting-better-at-ai-is-making-you-worse-at-product.html): New PMs who grow up on AI assistance may never develop the override muscle. The struggle AI eliminates is the same struggle that builds judgment.
- [Your AI Quality Problem Isn't Specifications. It's Taste.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/why-your-ai-outputs-are-mediocre-you-never-defined-good.html): Quality specifications get you from terrible to adequate. Taste gets you from adequate to good. The two are distinct problems and most advice conflates them.
- [Everyone Says Human Skills Will Matter. They're Right About One of Them.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/everyone-says-human-skills-will-matter-they-re-right-about-one-of-them.html): Of the six "AI-proof" human skills, only judgment actually scales in demand. The others remain stable. Investing in judgment is the rational career bet.
- [Your PM Job Is Six Jobs. You're Offloading the Wrong Half.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/your-pm-job-is-six-jobs-you-re-offloading-the-wrong-half.html): Every PM skill has a mechanical half (now free via AI) and a judgment half (now exposed). Most PMs are offloading the half they should be developing.
- [The PM Skills Map, Redrawn for AI](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/the-pm-skills-map-redrawn-for-ai.html): The four PM senses haven't changed, but what counts within each has. A reframing of the product management skill landscape for an AI-augmented world.
- [You're Not Leveraging AI. You're Leveraging a Fast Typewriter.](https://appliedcraft.blog/posts/you-re-not-leveraging-ai-you-re-leveraging-a-fast-typewriter.html): Four levels of AI leverage, plus a Level 0 of things to protect from AI entirely. Most PMs operate at Level 1 and call it mastery.

## About

Applied Craft is written by Sanidhya Khilnani, a product builder who has spent years shipping software at scale. The blog is deliberately small, deliberately opinionated, and updated with essays that each take a clear position.
